question: Why is the equivalent resistance of a parallel combination of resistors less than the smallest individual resistance? Give reason.

options.A: The equivalent resistance is less because current has to pass through the resistors one after another.
options.B: The equivalent resistance equals the sum of all resistances because the same current flows through every branch.
options.C: The equivalent resistance equals the smallest individual resistance because only one branch carries current.
options.D: A parallel combination provides multiple paths for current; hence $\dfrac{1}{R_p}$ is greater than the reciprocal of any individual resistance, making $R_p$ less than the smallest resistance.
